title: De legibus Angliae, ca. 1390
shelf_note: Bracton's De legibus, a medieval English legal manuscript. Medieval law is outside the core esoteric traditions but within the library's remit of historical primary sources. No collection is assigned.
structure_note: This is a heavily abbreviated Gothic manuscript, so the printed_backsteps (72) and printed_repeats (105) come from misattributed numbers, not a scan splice. The OCR tags page-num 73 on both 148 and 149 (the pencil folio '73' appears in both frames, at the edge of the opening). On 150 it invents page-num 154, which appears nowhere in the image (O16). The leaves themselves run in sequence.

book_verdict: The OCR of this abbreviated Gothic manuscript does not transcribe the leaf. It writes a plausible Latin paraphrase with invented words ('canes', 'spiritualis', 'in lapis', 'Henry the Fourth'), and the translation renders them fluently. An expert would reject it on sight. It should be held or re-OCRed with a lane suited to abbreviated legal manuscripts.

title: Theses de febre hectica
shelf_note: Disputation theses on hectic fever (1584, e-rara). Early modern medicine fits the early-modern-science remit. No tradition or collection is assigned.
structure_note: 12 pages, 11 OCR'd: likely a blank or a title verso. The one backstep comes from thesis numbers misread as page numbers. Note that the printed thesis number 'LXVIII' on page 6 is the printer's error for XXVIII.

title: rDo rje gro lod gnam lcags 'bar ba
shelf_note: A Dorje Drolo sadhana/ritual manuscript (Gangtey collection via BL EAP). Content matches the title: Drolo, the eight vidyadharas, Padmasambhava's manifestations, and the numbered ritual sections.
structure_note: Each image is a board with three pecha leaves (I5). Image 7 shows three rectos (with ༄༅། and margin folio numbers); images 6 and 8 show versos. Consecutive leaves are therefore split across photographs: page 7 holds sections 6-9 while page 8's middle leaf holds section 5. Reading order across the record is non-linear. Only 47 of 202 pages are translated. The OCR omits the marginal leaf numbers that would let a reader re-order.

book_verdict: The OCR and translation are serviceable for a Drolo ritual text. Deity names and ritual sections come through, with small slips (Yama rendered as Yamantaka). title: Alle de wercken
shelf_note: Jacob Cats' collected works (Amsterdam 1658), a BPH holding. These pages come from 'Weduwe' and the index to the Christian Housewife. Dutch moral verse is peripheral to the esoteric core but belongs to the partner's holdings.
structure_note: The catalogue language is 'Latin', but the text is Dutch verse; only the footnotes are Latin (I7). Each image is an unsplit two-page spread (printed pp. 192-193, 194-195), so one record holds two printed pages (I3). Printed backsteps and repeats follow from the spread numbering 'NNN-NNN' and the index pages. The run is in sequence (192 to 195, then the Tafel).
